sections.h: Quiet and cool decides whether a miner comes home
p: {imp_iv_cmv5n9msd0000vg1aqz1h7soi} needs a miner silent enough that it won't wake the family. {imp_iv_cmpltzezd0000if044cfutnmo} wants a bigger unit for better block odds, and the only thing holding them back is the noise in the house. {imp_iv_cmpn6ntlh0000l40477qxkhsx} checks how much heat every device puts out, because heat is a problem where they live in Florida.

These shoppers run miners in bedrooms, offices and shared living space, with nowhere to hide a loud box. If they can't tell how loud or how hot a miner runs, they don't buy it, so the store should answer that before they ask.

sections.h: They mine for the chance of one big win
p: {imp_iv_cmpomddzs0002js047o7vx2fe} dreams of waking up one morning to a block they found alone. {imp_iv_cmpltzezd0000if044cfutnmo} kept going after a friend hit a block, and {imp_iv_cmv5naq9r0000vgmu9qe5f7hs} remembers a small home miner that won one.
The fun is the long shot, and real block wins keep that hope going. Stories of small rigs that hit a block sell harder than specs do.

imp_iv_cmv5n9mtw0000vg21hfila9o7.who: Intermediate home miner running about 15 small Bitaxe/NerdQaxe-class miners (~50 TH/s) in the basement, shopping for the next miners to reach 100 TH/s
imp_iv_cmv5n9mtw0000vg21hfila9o7.job: Grow the fleet from 50 to 100 TH/s in $200-300 steps at about $20-25 per terahash.

imp_iv_cmv5nakw00000vgk7cx97ohwp.name: Matthew S.
imp_iv_cmv5nakw00000vgk7cx97ohwp.who: A Marine veteran who runs a basement fleet of Bitcoin and Scrypt home miners and is shopping for a replacement after their NerdQaxe++ sparked and died.
imp_iv_cmv5nakw00000vgk7cx97ohwp.job: Keep a cool, safe basement fleet running, get the dead 6 TH/s miner replaced and add a few more miners before calling the setup done.
imp_iv_cmv5nakw00000vgk7cx97ohwp.stopped: Their RMA form for the miner that threw sparks got no reply for about a week, so the replacement is on hold.
imp_iv_cmv5nakw00000vgk7cx97ohwp.alternatives: They checked other unnamed sites for the best deal on a replacement.

imp_iv_cmv5nel1x0000vgs7prexo4ej.name: Ted D.
imp_iv_cmv5nel1x0000vgs7prexo4ej.who: New home miner on a first Hammer Thor PS2, bought on sale from HeliumDeploy, who switches between Quai, Bitcoin Cash and Bitcoin to learn
imp_iv_cmv5nel1x0000vgs7prexo4ej.job: Learn how mining works on one budget miner, push it as hard as is safe, and maybe buy a second of the same model.
imp_iv_cmv5nel1x0000vgs7prexo4ej.stopped: Trying the alternative OS failed after two hours and they feared they had bricked the miner, and they found no YouTube help to fix it.
imp_iv_cmv5nel1x0000vgs7prexo4ej.alternatives: They first looked at Bitaxe models, then chose the Hammer Thor after a YouTube review, the sale price and the higher terahash.

imp_iv_cmv5n9msd0000vg1aqz1h7soi.name: Emilio V.
imp_iv_cmv5n9msd0000vg1aqz1h7soi.who: Solo home miner in Italy running an Avalon (address hidden), NerdOctaxe, NerdQaxe, Bitaxe Gamma and a Bitfortunate BS2, shopping for another quiet miner to heat a room
imp_iv_cmv5n9msd0000vg1aqz1h7soi.job: Heat each floor of the house with quiet miners that also take a shot at a solo block, all managed from one firmware.
imp_iv_cmv5n9msd0000vg1aqz1h7soi.stopped: A dead NerdOctaxe power brick has gone unanswered by support, and the Avalon Q is over budget and sold out.
imp_iv_cmv5n9msd0000vg1aqz1h7soi.alternatives: Looked at replacement power bricks from Bitronics/Victronix for about 70 euros, and checked Bosscoin and Red Panda YouTube reviews for noise.

imp_iv_cmvfjrcvm0000vgjmtn35mk4y.name: John M.
imp_iv_cmvfjrcvm0000vgjmtn35mk4y.who: Former QA manager at a Fortune 500 company, now out of work, who bought a Hammer DC08 Scrypt miner and already runs an Avalon Mini 3 (about 7 TH/s)
imp_iv_cmvfjrcvm0000vgjmtn35mk4y.job: Learn Scrypt and merge mining hands-on and gather data before possibly paying to host miners in a mining farm instead of at home
imp_iv_cmvfjrcvm0000vgjmtn35mk4y.stopped: The D.08 hashed far below its advertised rate and an RMA went unanswered for over a week, so buying from the store again now feels risky
imp_iv_cmvfjrcvm0000vgjmtn35mk4y.alternatives: Chose the DC08 over the DC06, later wished they had bought the Fluminer for more hashrate per watt, and turned down the Magic Miner 40T over its power draw

imp_iv_cmvfk3wqj0003vg0hv5j60hy9.name: Basement Bitaxe miner
imp_iv_cmvfk3wqj0003vg0hv5j60hy9.who: Quebec home miner running six Bitaxes and a Hammer in a cold basement, shopping for a miner above 40 TH/s
imp_iv_cmvfk3wqj0003vg0hv5j60hy9.job: Add a lot more hashrate at good efficiency, without a big jump in power draw or cost.
imp_iv_cmvfk3wqj0003vg0hv5j60hy9.stopped: Big new miners aren't proven yet and draw more power, firmware updates have bricked a miner before, US import fees add cost, and the store's Canada stock is often sold out.
imp_iv_cmvfk3wqj0003vg0hv5j60hy9.alternatives: Building their own miner from spare parts using YouTube tutorials, last-minute no-reserve eBay auctions, Facebook Marketplace deals found with ChatGPT, and Chinese vendors.

imp_iv_cmvfk4kaw000mvg0h4pgx4x6x.name: Solar lottery miner
imp_iv_cmvfk4kaw000mvg0h4pgx4x6x.who: Florida ex-Antminer miner who now runs small miners on solar and ordered a Thor P2 and a NerdOctaxe from HeliumDeploy
imp_iv_cmvfk4kaw000mvg0h4pgx4x6x.job: Run a couple of efficient miners on about 400 watts of solar for a shot at a solo block, while venting their heat out of the house
imp_iv_cmvfk4kaw000mvg0h4pgx4x6x.stopped: The order shipped a different miner than the one paid for, and weeks of waiting mean they haven't placed a second order
imp_iv_cmvfk4kaw000mvg0h4pgx4x6x.alternatives: Weighed two Thor P2s against one Harlo B30 and the NerdOctaxe, retired their old Antminers, and searched Maker's World for cooling shrouds

imp_iv_cmvfk2dy4000dvgyg559qt5kh.name: Philip S.
imp_iv_cmvfk2dy4000dvgyg559qt5kh.who: Hobby miner in Adelaide, Australia, running an S19, two Bitaxes and three Nerds in a hot garage, who was shopping for the 40T and then a Thor P2
imp_iv_cmvfk2dy4000dvgyg559qt5kh.job: Add about 10 to 40 terahash to a home garage setup without raising the power bill much.
imp_iv_cmvfk2dy4000dvgyg559qt5kh.stopped: Checkout would not accept the Australian address, the 40T had a two-month wait at about a thousand dollars with no local support, nobody could be found running the company behind the store, and the shipping quote they asked for never came.
imp_iv_cmvfk2dy4000dvgyg559qt5kh.alternatives: Bought the Thor P2 from Altair, which was a registered company with live chat and a price drop, and shipped it the next day.

imp_iv_cmventjey0000vgaov330hior.name: Mike A.
imp_iv_cmventjey0000vgaov330hior.who: Home hobby miner on Long Island running four Bitaxe 602s and Thor-class miners in the basement, shopping for low-power Bitcoin lottery miners
imp_iv_cmventjey0000vgaov330hior.job: Lottery-mine Bitcoin at home as a low-power hobby, grow slowly, and get his young kids interested in the technology.
imp_iv_cmventjey0000vgaov330hior.stopped: Doesn't want to spend much right now and the NerdOctaxe he wants is out of stock.
imp_iv_cmventjey0000vgaov330hior.alternatives: Bought a 3D-printed tower and fan on eBay because it was cheap, and looked elsewhere for the out-of-stock NerdOctaxe without saying where.

pinned.title: Shoppers need to know it's quiet enough
pinned.move: Put a plain noise and heat note on every miner's product page, right next to the price, saying how loud it runs and whether it can sit in a living space.
pinned.ask: Where in your home will this miner run, and how quiet does it need to be for you to keep it there?

chat.Why does noise matter so much to them?: Their miners run in bedrooms, offices and shared homes with no separate room to put them in, so anything loud just won't fly.
chat.How should I show it?: Show it the way the YouTubers they trust do: a sound reading taken next to the miner and a plain comparison, not a vague 'quiet' label.

pinned.why: In 24 of 109 interviews, shoppers raised this: the miner has to be quiet and cool enough to live in the house without bothering the family.

email.subject: Shoppers need to know it's quiet enough
email.pre: In 24 of 109 interviews, shoppers raised this: the miner has to be quiet and cool enough to live in the house without bothering the family.
email.head: Shoppers need to know it's quiet enough
email.move: Put a plain noise and heat note on every miner's product page, right next to the price, saying how loud it runs and whether it can sit in a living space.
